title: 存储的“下一个富矿”，突然不香了？
content: CXL (Compute Express Link) is emerging as a critical data-center technology in 2026 amid soaring DDR5 memory prices driven by AI demand. Unlike HBM, CXL enables memory pooling and expansion across servers via high-speed interconnects, allowing cost-effective scaling without overprovisioning CPU-attached DRAM. Major cloud providers including Meta and Google are deploying CXL to repurpose existing memory and reduce infrastructure costs. However, leading memory manufacturers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron have abandoned self-developed CXL controller commercialization, pivoting to third-party chip designers like Montage Technology, Microchip, and Marvell—strengthening independent controller vendors' market position ahead of anticipated mass adoption in 2027.

content: On July 25, OpenAI experienced a simultaneous outage affecting its API, ChatGPT, and Codex services, with 31 components degrading for nearly two hours. This marked 17 consecutive days of operational issues since July 9, ranging from degraded performance to major outages. The disruption is particularly significant for Codex programming agents, where interrupted tasks can cause project failures. The incident highlights growing enterprise risks from AI dependency, as API outages now halt production systems rather than merely disrupting chat experiences. This is accelerating demand for multi-model failover architectures and creating opportunities for alternative providers, including Chinese models, to capture overflow demand—provided they can match reliability under comparable loads.

title: 逛了9小时泡泡玛特乐园，我终于懂了段永平为什么说拿10年不卖
content:
A POP MART investor spent 9 hours at the company's urban theme park with his child, finding meticulous attention to detail throughout—from high-quality IP installations and carnival games with "never leave empty-handed" rules to immersive 4D theater and live character performances. The experience validated strong user engagement and emotional connection that drives repeat visits.

Investor Duan Yongping recently reversed his previous skepticism, becoming POP MART's second-largest shareholder with over 102 million shares and stating he likely won't sell for 10 years. His reasoning centers on three factors: a proven platform-based business model extending beyond blind boxes to full IP lifecycle monetization, strong corporate culture led by founder Wang Ning, and high long-term profit visibility—with some projections suggesting 50%+ probability of surpassing Disney's profits in 20 years.
